issues.legal_issue: Acquisition under the statutory scheme is invalid when the required prior requisition under that same scheme was absent, and a later requisition order made retrospectively does not cure the defect.
material_facts: The land and building had been requisitioned for defence use under a different legal authority.
An acquisition order under the applicable statutory scheme was made before any requisition order under that scheme.
A later order purporting to requisition the land under that scheme was assigned an effective date before the acquisition order.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was invalid because the statutory power to acquire applied only to land requisitioned under that same scheme, and the later retrospective requisition could not validate the earlier acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4 of the Assam Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948, make requisition under section 3 a prerequisite to acquisition under section 4. A requisition under another authority does not satisfy that condition, and a later order purporting to operate retrospectively cannot validate an acquisition made without the prerequisite. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.statutory_land_acquisition: The proceeding concerns an order acquiring land under a statutory land-acquisition scheme.
predicates.acquisition_authority_requires_prior_sch: The applicable acquisition authority permits acquisition only of land previously requisitioned under the same scheme.
predicates.effective_prior_scheme_requisition: A valid requisition under that scheme was in effect before the acquisition order was made.

issues.definition: When a statutory land-acquisition proceeding requires a prior requisition under the same scheme and none was effectively in place before acquisition, the acquisition order is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory bar on challenging orders made in exercise of statutory powers does not prevent a challenge to an acquisition order made without an essential statutory prerequisite.
material_facts: The acquisition order was made before any effective requisition under the statutory scheme that authorized acquisition only of land so requisitioned.
The governing Act contained a clause barring court challenges to decisions or orders made in exercise of powers conferred by or under that Act.
The affected owners challenged the validity of the acquisition, and the objection was considered in the statutory reference proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The statutory bar did not prevent the objection because the acquisition order, made without the required prior requisition, was not made in exercise of a power conferred by or under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Assam Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948, bars challenges only to decisions or orders made in exercise of a power conferred by or under the Act. Because section 4 authorized acquisition only of land requisitioned under section 3, an acquisition order made without an effective section 3 requisition did not fall within that bar. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.challenge_to_statutory_acquisition_order: A person challenges an order acquiring land under a statutory scheme.
predicates.statutory_bar_limited_to_orders_within_c: The applicable statutory bar covers only decisions or orders made in exercise of powers conferred by or under the scheme.
predicates.required_acquisition_prerequisite_absent: An essential condition for exercising the acquisition power was not satisfied when the acquisition order was made.

issues.definition: When an acquisition order is challenged, the statutory bar covers only orders within the powers conferred, and an essential prerequisite was absent, the bar does not prevent the challenge.
